images.caption: Figure 2:Typical Robotic Harness Paradigms.(1)Tool/code-as-policyharnesses leverage frontier models for high-level planning while relying on predefined tools or generated code for action execution. (2)Model-as-policyharnesses delegate action generation to specialized policy models. (3)Frontier-model-as-policyharnesses directly generate robot actions using frontier models. All three paradigms operate within a closed-loop framework, differing primarily in how robot actions are generated.

Figure 4:Overview of Embo-Harness.Embo-Harness is designed to leverage the model’s native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, failure-derived skills, or action priors. The harness takes task instructions and high-resolution visual observations as inputs to GPT-6-Astra with xhigh reasoning effort. The frontier model produces short, fixed-length chunks of absolute end-effector (EEF) actions. Short multi-action sequences and VLA refinement are further integrated as tools to enhance manipulation performance. Zoom in for best view of the demos.

Figure 5:Real-world robotic setup for Embo-Harness.Our setup consists of a Franka Research 3 (FR3) robot arm equipped with a Robotiq 2F-85 gripper, a wrist-mounted ZED Mini camera, and an external ZED 2 camera. We illustrate the objects and workspace used for real-world tabletop manipulation tasks.

Figure 8:Visualization of Real-World Rollout Demos Produced by Embo-Harness (Zoom in for best view).On the left is the view from the third-person camera, and on the right is the one from the wrist camera.
